content: The document titled Tuberculosis Prevention and Care Among Refugees and Other Populations in Humanitarian Settings: An Interagency Field Guide was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2022. It provides comprehensive guidance on addressing tuberculosis (TB) in vulnerable populations, particularly refugees and those affected by humanitarian emergencies. The guide emphasizes the importance of TB prevention and care in settings where poverty, overcrowding, undernutrition, and limited access to healthcare create conditions that facilitate the spread of TB. The publication is a collaborative effort between the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), and WHO. It introduces innovative strategies and updated approaches to TB prevention and care, tailored to the unique challenges of humanitarian settings. The guide also highlights the role of global research and digital technologies in improving TB diagnosis, treatment, and care. It aims to serve as a practical tool for healthcare providers and organizations working in humanitarian settings, with the ultimate goal of reducing suffering and deaths caused by this preventable and curable disease. The foreword acknowledges the increasing number of concurrent humanitarian emergencies in recent years, which have had profound social and economic impacts. Vulnerable populations, such as refugees and internally displaced persons, face significant health risks, including TB, which remains one of the leading infectious disease killers globally. The guide aligns with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which emphasizes equality, non-discrimination, and the principle of leaving no one behind. It also supports the United Nations' commitment to ending the TB epidemic by 2030. The document includes detailed annexes covering various aspects of TB care, such as drug quantification, program performance, supervision checklists, communication strategies, monitoring indicators, digital technologies, case definitions, treatment follow-up, and management of treatment interruptions. It also provides guidance on community health worker tasks, specimen collection and transport, drug resistance treatment options, people-centered care, adverse drug effects, and preventive treatment. The glossary defines key terms related to humanitarian settings, TB care, and vulnerable populations, ensuring clarity and consistency in the use of terminology. It also outlines the principles of equity, human rights, and protection, which are central to addressing the needs of displaced and marginalized populations. The guide acknowledges the contributions of numerous experts and organizations, including WHO, CDC, UNHCR, and other international agencies. It reflects a collaborative effort to address the complex challenges of TB prevention and care in humanitarian settings, with a focus on evidence-based practices and sustainable solutions.
